title: March warmth had positive links to reported absolute beech-larch date gaps in four Swiss samples in 1961-2020
abstract: We tested the link between March warmth and the absolute gap between beech leaf unfolding and larch needle emergence. Four Swiss region-period samples used 4,450 paired station-years at 94 fixed stations in 1961-2020. Models controlled station, time, winter and April warmth, with equal annual weights. March slopes were 1.89-2.20 days per C. All four eight-test sampling intervals were above zero. Stricter coverage, station trends and short serial-dependence checks kept this result. Sharp fixed-design bounds for two-day errors in each event date permit both March slope signs in three samples. The fourth lower bound is only 0.027 days per C. The absolute outcome tests separation without requiring a species order. This follow-up uses the same records as a prior signed-gap study, not independent biological data. Missing visits, selected complete pairs and coarse weather limit inference. These associations do not show a causal climate effect, long-term synchrony loss or ecological harm. Pollution and daily extremes were not tested. Code, evidence tables, source hashes, checks and a figure are included.

display.caption: Absolute date-gap slopes in four Swiss samples. Blue lines are eight-test sampling intervals. Brown lines are sharp fixed-design bounds for two-day errors in each event date; they are not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Same source records, panel construction and seasonal design; new absolute outcome and sharp transformed-outcome bounds. Not independent biological validation.
